findings.rootCause: FrontierStatisticsGeneration.validateShard called shard.close() when a shard's header did not match the new manifest. A new generation maps every shard it shares with the live generation by RETAINING the live generation's SharedShard (retainSharedShard) instead of reopening the file. A rejected publication (for example a manifest whose baseEpoch/coveredEpoch/maximumTermId disagrees with a reused shard) therefore unmapped a shard that the live generation and every query lease on it still read. The live generation then threw IllegalStateException('Frontier statistics shard is closed') on every access, and the underlying MappedByteBuffer was cleaned, so an already obtained reader could touch unmapped memory.
findings.change: validateShard now only throws. The caller's existing catch calls sharedShard.release(failure), which drops only the new generation's reference and closes the mapping once no generation maps it any more, so a freshly opened shard is still closed on rejection and a shared one stays mapped for the live generation. Sound because SharedShard reference counting already owns the mapping lifecycle; the close in validateShard was a second, unconditional owner.

findings.id: 3.6.5-bR (b4 follow-up: bound-key leaf product returned a NONE sampled point zero)
findings.rootCause: FrontierOmniIndex.estimateBridge answers a join whose key component is bound on one side by the bound-key shortcut: the product of two leaf estimates (one leaf bound to the join key), marked decisive so the reverse orientation is never consulted. productEstimate always labelled the product fallbackReason NONE. When the bound leaf was a SAMPLED zero (no sampled row matched, interval [0, upper>0], confidence 0) the planner received a NONE point 0 with confidence 0, the exact defect b3 removed for sampled bridges (confirmed: correlated data, p7.p = p8.o gives point 0, upper 882,000, confidence 0.0 both from FrontierOmniIndex and from the planner-facing FrontierMappedStatistics). The same shortcut also turned a DECLINED leaf (FrontierLeafEstimate.unavailable: point 1, upper MAX, reachable since 3.6.6b budget declines) into a NONE product.
findings.change: New FrontierOmniIndex.leafProduct(left, right): a declined input propagates its typed fallback reason; a product whose point is 0 while its own upper is > 0 becomes a typed CONFIDENCE_TOO_WIDE unknown; exact zeros (upper 0, e.g. a complete cell or disjoint bound keys) and positive products are unchanged. Because both orientations compute the same product, the result is final: BridgeResult.symmetricUnknown (weak=false) and decisive() is now '!weak' (exact, strong or orientation-symmetric), which is identical to the old 'available && !weak' for every pre-existing construction (unavailable results carry weak=true). Downstream, FrontierMappedStatistics falls back to centers / Fast-AGMS (which since b4 types a zero median as unknown) and packed consumers to independence. This matches roadmap 4.3 (unknown is neither 1 nor 0). The declined-leaf branch has no dedicated failing test (it needs a budget-exhausted scan inside a bound-key probe, which no test seam exposes); it is the same invariant enforced by the same helper.
testsAdded: FrontierOmniBridgeOrientationTest#boundJoinKeyWithASampledZeroLeafIsATypedUnknownInsteadOfAPointZero (all role pairs involving the bound predicate component; omni and planner-facing mapped estimates; exact must stay inside any NONE interval)
